Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Consumer Goods Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Consumer Goods' Q3 results. With me on the call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Reynolds.  

John Reynolds:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Apex Consumer Goods delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover five key aspects:  
1. Overall company performance highlights.  
2. Geographic performance: developed versus emerging markets.  
3. Gross margin percentage.  
4. A&P spend and ROI.  
5. Outlook for the remainder of the year, including organic sales growth guidance.  

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Michael Chen:  
Thank you, John. As John mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $6.6 billion, representing an 8.2% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by strategic pricing, mix management, supply chain productivity, and commodity hedges. Operating income was $1.2 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.42. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me start with the overall company performance highlights. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 FY2024 earnings call for Apex Consumer Goods. As your CFO, I'm thrilled to kick off the highlights with what I can confidently call a standout quarter, delivering robust top- and bottom-line results amid a resilient yet dynamic CPG landscape. We reported net sales of $6.6 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year, handily beating our guidance midpoint and marking our ninth consecutive quarter of organic growth. Organic net sales—stripping out the 1.5% impact from FX headwinds and the 2.1% boost from our recent acquisition of EcoSnacks, a leader in plant-based savory alternatives—grew 7.6%, driven by a healthy mix of 4.2% volume/mix and 3.4% pricing actions. This outpaced the broader CPG category, which per IRI data grew just 3.1% in measured channels.  

Diving deeper into the P&L, adjusted diluted EPS came in at $1.42, a 12.5% increase from last year, exceeding our $1.35-$1.38 whisper range. This was fueled by gross margin expansion to 48.2%—up 170 basis points year-over-year—thanks to our multi-year supply chain productivity program, which delivered $185 million in savings this quarter alone. Core drivers included optimized procurement of key commodities like cocoa and palm oil, where we locked in hedges ahead of the Ivory Coast supply disruptions, and a 15% reduction in ocean freight costs via our strategic shift to nearshoring in Mexico for North American SKUs. Operating margin hit 18.4%, up 140 bps, as SG&A leverage came in at 23.9% of sales, reflecting disciplined zero-based budgeting and a 10% headcount optimization in indirect functions without impacting go-to-market velocity.  

By segment, our Nutrition & Wellness division—home to powerhouse brands like VitalGlow protein bars and our newly launched keto-friendly NutriFuel line—led the charge with 11.3% organic growth, capturing share in the high-velocity $28 billion U.S. health snacking category. Household penetration rose 2.3 points per Nielsen, outpacing category leader Clif Bar, as we leaned into e-commerce, now 22% of divisional sales via Amazon and our D2C platform. Beauty & Personal Care grew 6.8% organically, with premiumization shining through: our HydraPure skincare range, inspired by clean beauty trends akin to The Ordinary's disruption, saw 25% repeat purchase rates and drove 4% market share gains in measured beauty per SPINS data. Household Essentials rounded out at 5.9% organic growth, bolstered by value-pack innovations in our EverClean laundry pods, which countered private label pressure—now at 28% category share—through superior cleaning efficacy claims validated by third-party lab tests.  

Regionally, North America, our largest market at 52% of sales, delivered 9.1% organic growth, with market share up 60 bps to 14.2% across our portfolio, per Circana totals. Consumers traded down less in our premium tiers, reflecting sticky loyalty in a 4.1% inflationary environment. EMEA grew 6.4% organically despite softer UK volumes from excise tax hikes on sugary beverages—think similar to PepsiCo's dynamics there—offset by double-digit gains in plant-based dairy alternatives in Germany and France, where we're gaining on Danone with our Oatly-licensed extensions. APAC was the star at 12.7% organic, led by 18% growth in China premium snacks, fueled by our Tmall flagship store relaunch and KOL partnerships yielding 3x ROI. LATAM rounded out at 5.2%, resilient against Argentina's hyperinflation via localized pricing and our JVs with local bottlers.  

Strategically, we're executing on our "Growth Accelerator 2025" roadmap with precision. R&D investments hit $220 million, or 4.6% of sales, unlocking 17 new product launches, including our zero-sugar electrolyte line targeting the $15 billion functional beverage space—a direct response to Prime's viral success and Gatorade's share erosion. Sustainability remains core: 68% of our portfolio now carries eco-certifications, driving a 14% uplift in millennial Gen Z preference scores per Kantar, and our regenerative agriculture program with soy farmers in Brazil reduced Scope 3 emissions by 22%. Digitally, our AI-powered revenue growth management tool—integrated with Black Book data—optimized pricing elasticity models, contributing 1.2 points to organic growth. On M&A, the EcoSnacks tuck-in is performing ahead of plan, with $45 million in run-rate synergies by year-end.  

Balance sheet-wise, we generated $1.1 billion in operating cash flow, up 16%, enabling $650 million in share repurchases and a 10% dividend hike to $0.78 per share—our 28th consecutive increase. Net debt to EBITDA stands at a pristine 2.1x, giving us ample dry powder for bolt-ons in adjacencies like pet nutrition, where we're eyeing opportunities amid Mars' dominance.  

In summary, Q3 underscores Apex's ability to navigate volume softness in staples—down 1.2% industry-wide—through innovation, productivity, and consumer-centric agility. We're raising full-year guidance: organic sales now 7-8%, adjusted EPS $5.65-$5.75, and gross margin at least 250 bps expansion.  

Now, let me dive into our geographic performance for Q3, with a particular focus on the divergence between our developed and emerging market portfolios. As you know, our CPG portfolio—spanning personal care, beverages, snacks, and household essentials under brands like FreshGlow skincare, Quench hydration drinks, and NutriBite snacks—continues to benefit from our balanced global footprint. Geographically, developed markets account for 62% of our net sales, or $4.1 billion in the quarter, while emerging markets represent 38%, or $2.5 billion. On an organic constant-currency basis, this split delivered total company organic growth of 6.2%, but the story is one of resilience in developed markets offsetting robust expansion in emerging ones.  

Starting with developed markets, which include North America, Western Europe, and Australia/New Zealand, we posted organic sales growth of 2.1%, a slight deceleration from 3.5% in Q2, reflecting softer consumer demand amid persistent inflation and downtrading pressures. In North America, our largest market at 38% of total sales, organic growth came in at 1.8%, driven by a 4% volume uptick in value-oriented essentials like our NutriBite protein bars and Quench low-sugar variants, which gained 110 basis points of market share per IRI multi-outlet scans. However, pricing moderated to +3% as retailers like Walmart and Kroger pushed back on everyday low-price (EDLP) programs amid 4-5% CPI food-at-home inflation. Margins held steady at 22.4%, up 50 bps year-over-year, thanks to our $150 million in supply chain savings from precision fermentation tech in beverage production and optimized palm oil sourcing via our blockchain traceability platform.  

Western Europe was flat organically at 0.2% growth, weighed down by a 2% volume decline in premium beauty—FreshGlow's anti-aging serums saw some softness as L'Oréal and Beiersdorf ramped promotions—but offset by 3% pricing in household care. Regulatory tailwinds from the EU Green Deal helped us launch three eco-refill packs, boosting market share by 80 bps in Nielsen data. Overall, developed market adjusted operating margins expanded 120 bps to 23.1%, fueled by our "Efficiency Edge" program, which includes AI-driven demand forecasting reducing inventory days by 15% to 45 days.  

Shifting to emerging markets, the growth engine hummed at 14.7% organic constant-currency growth, accelerating from 12.8% last quarter and contributing over 70% of our total organic sales lift. This reflects urbanization, rising middle-class incomes, and e-commerce penetration, now at 28% of sales versus 12% in developed markets. Asia-Pacific, 18% of total sales, surged 16.2%, led by India and China. In India, Quench's fortified hydration drinks grew 25% on distribution expansion to 1.2 million outlets via quick-commerce partners like Blinkit, capturing 250 bps share per Kantar data amid 40% category growth. China volumes jumped 12% post our RMB 500 million investment in direct-to-consumer via Tmall and Douyin, with premiumization—FreshGlow hyaluronic masks up 30%—driving mix benefits. Latin America, at 12% of sales, delivered 15.4% growth despite 8% FX headwinds; Brazil's NutriBite clean-label snacks hit 20% growth on PBM partnerships with Carrefour, while Mexico saw 18% uplift from nearshored production cutting lead times by 25%.  

Middle East & Africa (MEA) rounded out at 10.9% growth, with standout 22% in Saudi Arabia tied to Vision 2030 localization—our Jeddah plant now supplies 70% of Gulf demand, slashing duties and boosting EBITDA margins to 18.5%. Emerging market margins compressed 80 bps to 20.3% due to input cost volatility (e.g., 15% cocoa spike), but our forward commodity hedges and regional hubs mitigated 60% of exposure.  

Strategically, this bifurcation underscores our "Dual Gear" playbook: in developed markets, we're leaning into shopper loyalty via Club programs—loyalty penetration up 15% to 45%—and sustainability creds, like 100% recyclable Quench bottles ahead of 2025 plastic pact goals. In emerging, we're accelerating "Market Multiplier" initiatives: $800 million capex for five new plants in India, Indonesia, and Nigeria; digital go-to-market with hyperlocal D2C apps hitting 50 million MAUs; and tailored innovation, like halal-certified NutriBite for MEA and low-water FreshGlow for water-stressed LatAm.  

Looking ahead, we see developed markets stabilizing at 2-4% organic growth in FY24 as real incomes recover, while emerging accelerates to 15-17%, albeit with FX volatility—our 65% natural hedge via local sourcing provides resilience. Risks include U.S. recessionary pullback and LatAm elections, but our 14% ROIC target remains intact, with emerging markets pulling it higher to 16%. We're well-positioned to outpace peers like P&G and Unilever, who reported 4.5% and 5.1% organic growth last quarter.  

Turning now to our gross margin performance, which came in at 48.2% for the quarter—up 170 basis points year-over-year from 46.5% and 40 basis points sequentially from 47.8% in Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly gross margin expansion in the past five years and exceeded our guidance midpoint by 60 basis points. For the nine months year-to-date, we're at 47.6%, positioning us well to hit our full-year target of 48.0% plus or minus 50 basis points.  

Let me unpack the key drivers behind this performance, which reflect a combination of disciplined pricing, mix management, and structural cost efficiencies—hallmarks of our CPG playbook in this inflationary environment.  

Pricing and mix tailwinds contributed about 120 bps. Our strategic pricing actions across the portfolio added approximately 9% to net revenue growth this quarter, outpacing input cost inflation by 400 basis points. In North America, which represents 55% of our revenue, we realized full velocity recovery post-pricing on our core snack brands like Apex Crunch chips and VitalQuench beverages, with average unit retail (AUR) up 8.2% year-over-year. Premiumization played a big role here: high-margin organic and plant-based SKUs, such as our newly launched Apex Organics line, grew 18% in volume and now comprise 12% of North American snacking sales, delivering a 5-point mix benefit. This mirrors trends we've seen at peers like PepsiCo, where Frito-Lay's premium segments have driven similar margin leverage.  

In EMEA, pricing was up 11%, but softer than expected due to heightened promotional intensity amid the cost-of-living crisis—trade spend as a percentage of revenue ticked up to 22% from 20%. Still, our household essentials like Apex Clean detergents held firm, with margins expanding 90 bps to 45.2%, bolstered by everyday low-price (EDLP) strategies that preserved consumer loyalty without eroding AUR.  

Commodity and supply chain headwinds were mitigated, neutral to +30 bps. Input costs remained elevated, with cocoa prices up 25% year-to-date due to West African supply disruptions—impacting our chocolate confectionery segment—and palm oil volatile from El Niño weather patterns. Overall COGS inflation was 5.2%, down from 7.1% in Q2, thanks to our forward commodity hedging program, which locked in 70% of 2024 volumes at favorable rates.  

Regionally, Asia-Pacific faced the biggest commodity squeeze, with margins at 43.8% (down 20 bps YoY) due to higher dairy costs in our powdered beverage lines, reminiscent of Nestlé's challenges in Southeast Asia. However, we offset this through procurement savings: our supplier collaboration portal, powered by SAP Ariba, yielded $45 million in annualized savings, or 60 bps of margin accretion.  

Operational efficiencies and technical initiatives added +50 bps. Factory utilization hit 88%—up from 82% last year—driven by AI-optimized production scheduling in our 45 North American plants, reducing downtime by 15% and waste by 8% on high-velocity items like single-serve beverage packs. We're also advancing vertical integration: our new recycled PET resin facility in Mexico, now at 75% capacity, cuts packaging costs by 12% for VitalQuench bottles and supports our sustainability goals, appealing to Gen Z consumers who prioritize eco-friendly packaging.  

Supply chain resilience was key amid Red Sea disruptions; by dual-sourcing 80% of ocean freight from alternative routes via India and Vietnam, we limited logistics inflation to 2.5% versus the industry average of 6%, per NielsenIQ data. FX headwinds shaved 10 bps, primarily from a stronger USD impacting our 25% APAC revenue exposure.  

Looking ahead, we see sustained margin expansion as a competitive moat in CPG. Our 'Margin First' framework—prioritizing high-ROIC innovation, zero-based budgeting, and dynamic pricing analytics—positions us to outpace peers like Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive, who reported more modest 50-80 bps gains this quarter. We're targeting 100 bps of additional expansion in 2024 through ERP go-lives (Oracle Cloud in EMEA by Q2), sustainable sourcing (e.g., RSPO-certified palm oil at 95% coverage), and accelerating direct-to-consumer channels, where gross margins exceed 60%.  

That said, risks include potential U.S. labor strikes inflating wage costs and softening demand pressuring pricing elasticity. For Q4, we guide gross margins to 48.5-49.0%, with full-year confidence intact.  

Finally, before I hand over, a quick note on outlook, particularly organic sales growth for Q4 and FY2025. Organic sales growth remains our North Star metric here at Apex—it strips out the noise from FX, M&A, and divestitures to highlight the true health of our core brands across beverages, snacks, and household essentials. We're proud of delivering 6.2% organic growth in Q3, driven by pricing, volume/mix, and early momentum from innovations like PureVital.  

For Q4, we are guiding for organic sales growth of 3.5% to 4.5%. This reflects a sequential step-up from Q3 as we lap tougher comps from last year's supply chain recovery and capitalize on holiday seasonality. Pricing contribution: 1.8% to 2.2%. We've executed disciplined pricing across 70% of our North American portfolio, including a 4-6% list price increase on our flagship AquaSparkle hydration line and CrystalCrisp snacks, in response to lingering cocoa and PET resin inflation—which, per Bloomberg data, is still up 15% YoY. Elasticity has held in at -2.5x, better than the category average of -3.2x per IRI scans, thanks to our value-engineered packs like the $1.99 'Everyday Duo' bundles that protect household penetration.  

Volume/mix: 1.5% to 2.0%. We're forecasting modest volume recovery as consumers trade back from private label after a 18-month value shift. Our innovation pipeline is firing on all cylinders: the PureVital functional beverage line—think zero-sugar electrolytes with adaptogens—is already tracking +12% ACV in test markets, outpacing Gatorade's recent wellness extensions. Snacks volume should inflect positively off troughs, with our air-popped 'CrispAir' chips gaining 1.2 share points in salty snacks per Nielsen, driven by Gen Z-targeted TikTok campaigns yielding 25% higher conversion rates.  

Regionally: North America (65% of sales): 3.0% to 4.0% organic growth. We're outpacing IRI-measured CPG category growth of +1.5% through distribution gains—up 200 bps to 92% ACV for beverages—and e-comm acceleration. Amazon and Walmart+ fulfillment now covers 40% of our hydrate portfolio, with 18% YoY online sales growth amid a 22% category surge. Europe (20% of sales): 4.0% to 5.0%, benefiting from premiumization tailwinds. Our EcoPure household cleaners, with 98% bio-based formulas, are stealing share from Unilever's Domestos line, up 3 points in Euromonitor data, as EU sustainability regs like the Green Deal favor our low-water phosphate-free tech. Emerging Markets (15% of sales): 5.5% to 6.5%, led by LatAm and India. In Brazil, our affordable 'AquaEssentials' sachet packs are driving +8% volume amid Real depreciation, while India's rural distribution via 50,000 new Project Shakti micro-entrepreneurs mirrors P&G's playbook, targeting +15% HCP growth in underserved villages.  

For the full FY2025, we're raising our organic sales growth guidance to 4.0% to 5.0%, up from our prior 3.5-4.5% range. This implies a Q4 acceleration to offset any Q1 softness from Chinese New Year timing shifts. Year-to-date, we've delivered on track for the top end if consumer confidence holds. Key strategic insights: Share gains via superior innovation and NGS execution—our Net Growth Strategy focusing on '10X brands' like AquaSparkle (now #2 in sports drinks, +1.5 share vs. Powerade)—has unlocked 150 bps of market outperformance YTD per Kantar. We're investing $250M in R&D for 20+ SKUs, including plant-based snack reformulations to tap the $50B global alt-protein wave, akin to Mondelez's perfect snacks pivot.  

Balanced portfolio mix shift: Premium and health products now 35% of sales (up from 28% in FY23), delivering 200 bps of mix benefit. This premiumization is resilient even in downtrading environments—witness our +7% growth in 'PureVital' vs. flat mass-market juices. Supply chain resilience and tech initiatives: Post-2022 disruptions, our AI-driven demand sensing platform—powered by Blue Yonder, similar to PepsiCo's implementations—has reduced OOS rates to 4% from 12%, enabling velocity gains. We're also rolling out dynamic pricing algorithms in 15 markets, optimizing for real-time elasticity data from 500M+ loyalty app users. Macro and consumer tailwinds: U.S. real disposable income growth of +2.5% per BEA data supports at-home consumption, where CPG shines. Health & wellness trends persist—62% of consumers prioritizing 'functional benefits' per our proprietary surveys, aligning with NielsenIQ's +4% category forecast. E-comm and DTC channels grow to 12% of sales, with CLV up 22% via personalized recs.  

Of course, risks remain. Elevated interest rates could pressure lower-income households, potentially capping volume at the low end. Geopolitical tensions in cocoa supply (hello, Ivory Coast elections) and FX volatility—especially a stronger USD—are headwinds, though our 60/40 hedged book mitigates 80% exposure. Inflation receding to 2-3% globally per IMF should ease input costs, flowing 50% to margins.  

In summary, this guidance reflects confidence in our playbook: relentless consumer focus, bold innovation, and operational excellence. We're not just growing—we're gaining share in a +2% CPG universe, positioning Apex for sustained mid-single-digit compounding.  

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss our A&P investments, marketing, and brand performance.  

Lisa Patel:  
Thank you, Michael. We saw strong performance in our FreshGlow and Quench brands this quarter. Good afternoon, everyone. As we dive into our marketing investments, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our Advertising & Promotion, or A&P, spend and the strong ROI trajectory we're delivering. In the CPG space, where shelf space is finite and consumer loyalty is fiercely contested, disciplined A&P allocation is our lifeblood for driving volume, share gains, and long-term brand equity. We've continued to lean into data-driven precision here, navigating a dynamic environment marked by softening category demand in staples like household care amid persistent inflation pressures.  

Let me start with the numbers. For Q3, total A&P spend came in at $452 million, representing 11.8% of net sales—up 4% year-over-year on a constant currency basis, but flat as a percentage of sales versus Q3 2022. This reflects our commitment to maintaining investment levels in a tough macro, prioritizing efficiency over volume growth in spend. Year-to-date, we're at $1.32 billion, or 12.1% of sales, in line with our full-year guidance of 11.5-12.5%. Breaking it down further: Advertising, which includes consumer-facing media like TV, digital, and OOH, accounted for 42% of the total at $190 million, up 8% YoY driven by digital acceleration. Promotions—encompassing trade spend, shopper marketing, coupons, and loyalty programs—made up the balance at 58%, or $262 million, which was flat YoY as we optimized for better returns amid retailer pushback on funding rates.  

Now, turning to ROI—this is where our story shines. Using our proprietary Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) framework, augmented by Nielsen and IRI panel data, we track both short-term ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) and longer-term Marketing ROI (MROI), which incorporates halo effects like brand lift and repeat purchase velocity. Q3 aggregate MROI improved to 2.6x, up from 2.3x in Q3 2022 and a sequential lift from 2.5x in Q2. That's translating to approximately $1.18 billion in incremental revenue attributable to A&P—a 12% YoY increase. On ROAS specifically, we hit 3.8x overall, with performance channels leading the charge.  

Regionally, performance varied but trended positive across the board. In North America, which represents 55% of our A&P budget, spend rose 6% to $249 million, fueled by aggressive retail media network (RMN) investments via partnerships with Walmart Connect, Kroger Precision Marketing, and Target's Roundel. Here, our ROAS hit an impressive 4.5x, thanks to shoppable video ads on platforms like Walmart's VIZIO-powered CTV inventory. We saw particular strength in our FreshGlow laundry portfolio, where targeted display and sponsored search drove a 15% lift in ACV (All-Commodity Volume) share versus P&G's Tide, per Circana data. Trade promo efficiency also improved 10% via AI-optimized allowance negotiations, reducing slotting fees by 7% on average.  

In EMEA, 25% of spend at $113 million, we moderated growth to 2% YoY amid regulatory headwinds on HFSS (High Fat, Salt, Sugar) advertising. ROI held steady at 2.4x, bolstered by first-party data clean rooms with Tesco and Carrefour, enabling personalized email and app-based promos for our Zestify snack line. We shifted 10 percentage points more budget to DOOH (Digital Out-of-Home) in urban hubs like London and Paris, yielding 3.2x ROAS amid Eurozone consumer downtrading.  

APAC, our high-growth engine at 15% of spend ($68 million, up 12% YoY), delivered the standout 3.1x MROI. Digital dominance here—now 65% of regional A&P—powered this, with Tmall and JD.com live-streaming events for our GlowBright personal care range generating 6:1 ROAS during Singles' Day prep. We're also piloting generative AI for hyper-localized content in India via JioMart, testing dynamic pricing promos that boosted conversion rates by 22%.  

Finally, LatAm rounded out at 5% of spend ($22 million, up 3%), with 2.8x ROI despite FX volatility. Mercado Libre's sponsored products were key for our value-tier beverages, capturing share from Coca-Cola's Inca Kola in Brazil.  

Strategically, we're accelerating three technical initiatives to sustain this momentum. First, our AI-powered Attribution Engine, built on Google's Meridian and integrated with Snowflake for zero-party data, now attributes 85% of spend at the SKU-store-week level, uncovering $25 million in annual savings from underperforming linear TV buys. Second, we're scaling clean room collaborations with Amazon DSP and The Trade Desk for privacy-safe, cookieless targeting—early tests show 25% better incrementality on upper-funnel brand campaigns. Third, sustainability-linked A&P: 20% of Q3 digital creative highlighted our 'Planet Positive' packaging for FreshGlow, driving a 18% uplift in purchase intent among Gen Z per YouGov polls, with MROI at 3.5x.  

Looking forward, we expect Q4 A&P at 12-13% of sales, with MROI expanding to 2.7x+ as holiday RMN ramps and we launch incrementality holdouts on CTV. This positions us to gain 50 basis points of market share in core categories, outpacing peers like Unilever and Reckitt amid moderating promo inflation. Our recent marketing campaigns, including the Glow-Up campaign for FreshGlow, have resonated well with consumers. We are also excited about the launch of our new product, PureVital zero-sugar electrolytes, which is already generating positive feedback and tracking double-digit ACV distribution in test markets, contributing to share gains in the functional beverage segment.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. If you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.  

Emily Carter:  
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new Glow-Up marketing campaign and its impact on sales?  

Lisa Patel:  
Good morning, Emily. Absolutely, happy to elaborate. The Glow-Up campaign for FreshGlow skincare was a multi-channel push centered on our anti-aging serums and hyaluronic masks, leveraging RMN partnerships like Walmart Connect and digital CTV via VIZIO. We allocated about $35 million to it in Q3, focusing on shoppable video ads and personalized promos through first-party data clean rooms. The impact has been strong: it drove a 15% lift in ACV share for FreshGlow versus competitors like L'Oréal, per Circana, contributing roughly $120 million in incremental sales. ROAS came in at 4.2x, thanks to Gen Z targeting with sustainability messaging around our Planet Positive packaging, which boosted purchase intent by 18% in YouGov polls. We're scaling it into Q4 holidays for even more halo effects on repeat buys.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.  

David Lee:  
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?  

Michael Chen:  
Hi David, good question. Rising commodities like cocoa, up 25% YTD from West African disruptions, and palm oil volatility from El Niño remain top of mind. Our plan is multifaceted: we've hedged 70% of 2024 volumes at favorable rates, mitigating about 60% of exposure as seen in emerging markets. Procurement optimizations via SAP Ariba delivered $45 million in savings this quarter alone. We're advancing nearshoring, like our Mexico PET facility cutting packaging costs 12%, and precision fermentation for beverages saving $150 million. For Q4 and beyond, dynamic pricing analytics and AI demand forecasting will protect margins, targeting another 100 bps expansion in FY24 while flowing savings to innovation.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley.  

Rachel Kim:  
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?  

John Reynolds:  
Thanks, Rachel. Inflation at 4-5% CPI food-at-home continues to drive some downtrading, but our premium lines like HydraPure skincare and PureVital beverages are holding resilient. In developed markets, premiumization delivered a 5-point mix benefit in North America, with volumes up 18% for Apex Organics despite softer overall demand. Loyalty programs boosted penetration to 45%, and eco-credentials like 100% recyclable Quench bottles appeal to sticky segments. In emerging markets, urbanization and middle-class growth fueled 30% uplift in premium FreshGlow masks in China. Overall, health & wellness trends—62% of consumers prioritizing functional benefits—support mid-single-digit growth in premiums, outpacing mass-market softness.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Tom Harris with Barclays.  

Tom Harris:  
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?  

Lisa Patel:  
Hi Tom. E-commerce was a bright spot, now 22% of Nutrition & Wellness sales and accelerating to 28% in emerging markets versus 12% developed. In North America, Amazon and D2C drove 18% YoY growth for beverages, with Walmart+ covering 40% of hydrate portfolio amid 22% category surge. APAC led with Tmall/Douyin investments yielding 6:1 ROAS on live-streams for GlowBright, and hyperlocal apps hitting 50 million MAUs. Initiatives like generative AI on JioMart boosted conversions 22% in India. Overall, e-comm contributed 1.2 points to organic growth, with CLV up 22% via personalized recs—we're targeting 12% of total sales in FY25.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to John Reynolds for closing remarks.  

John Reynolds:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex Consumer Goods Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Geographic performance: developed vs. em: Developed markets (62% of sales, $4.1B) grew 2.1% organically, with NA at 1.8% and Western Europe flat at 0.2%, reflecting softer demand and inflation. Emerging markets (38%, $2.5B) surged 14.7% organically, led by APAC (16.2%), LATAM (15.4%), and MEA (10.9%), driven by urbanization and e-commerce. Outlook: developed 2-4%, emerging 15-17% for FY24.
aspect_summary.A&P (advertising & promotion) spend and: Q3 A&P spend $452M (11.8% of sales), +4% YoY CC; YTD $1.32B (12.1%), FY guidance 11.5-12.5%. MROI 2.6x (up from 2.3x), ROAS 3.8x, generating $1.18B incremental revenue. NA ROAS 4.5x, APAC MROI 3.1x. Q4: 12-13% of sales, MROI 2.7x+.
aspect_summary.Overall company performance highlights: Q3 net sales $6.6B (+8.2% YoY), organic 7.6% (4.2% volume/mix, 3.4% pricing), beating guidance. Adj EPS $1.42 (+12.5%). Gross margin 48.2% (+170bps). Segments: Nutrition & Wellness +11.3%, Beauty & Personal Care +6.8%, Household +5.9%. Regions: NA +9.1%, APAC +12.7%. Raised FY24 guidance: organic 7-8%, EPS $5.65-5.75, GM +250bps.
aspect_summary.Gross margin percentage: Q3 48.2% (+170bps YoY, +40bps QoQ), strongest in 5 years. YTD 47.6%, FY24 target 48.0% +/-50bps. Drivers: pricing/mix +120bps, efficiencies +50bps, hedging neutral to +30bps. Q4 guide 48.5-49.0%.
